payload.summary: Lagos pulses with an infectious, youth-driven Afro-fusion energy, where the streets hum to the beats of homegrown superstars like Rema, Burna Boy, CKay, and Mr Eazi, blending global trends with deeply rooted Nigerian rhythms. This vibrant metropolis is a sensory overload of sleek modern eateries, high-end brands, and a pop-culture saturation that mirrors its ambition and restless innovation, making every case feel like navigating the heart of a boiling, beating cultural revolution.

npc.archetype: Ex-Military Intelligence Officer Turned Private Investigator
npc.description: A wiry man in his late 40s with a faded green Nigerian Army jacket, his sleeves rolled up to reveal tattooed forearms. He sports a carefully groomed mustache and carries a well-worn leather satchel stuffed with files and a GlenfiddichDistilleryashtray he took as a souvenir from a military outpost. His eyes have that hardened Lagos sun-glare, forever scanning for the next angle.
npc.quote: In this city, trust is a luxury you can't afford and every alley has a price.
dialogue: You think Vogüéis just a restaurant? It’s where contracts get signed over grilled goat and palm wine.
These generals they wear stars on their shoulders, but they’re just men hiding behind bars and bullets.
When the heat hits and the generator dies, you’ll see who really survives — it ain’t the ones with titles.
eats_at: Al Habtoor Grand Resort, Autograph Collection

npc.description: A vibrant woman in her early 30s with a bright Ankara top and oversized sunglasses hanging off her head wrap. Her backpack is covered in stickers from My Roomconcerts and she always has a small recorder tucked in her ear, capturing the pulse of the streets. Her voice carries the rhythm of Lagos — fast, fluent, and fiercely observant.
npc.quote: If you ain’t dancing to Flexyor arguing with a street vendor, you ain’t living in Lagos.
dialogue: I covered the last real Afro-funk night at My Roombefore it turned into a corporate showcase — real music don’t need sponsors.
The system? It’s a broken tape loop — keeps playing the same corrupt story unless we hit rewind.
When the power cuts and the kids start drumming on old oil drums, that’s when you hear the city’s real voice.
eats_at: Al Habtoor Grand Resort, Autograph Collection

npc.archetype: Customs Broker with Side-Hustle Artifacts Trader
npc.description: A dapper man in his 50s with a tailored Agbada over a crisp shirt, gold chains glinting under the neon of the old Al Habtoor Grand Resort. He smells faintly of rare incense and carries a walking stick that doubles as a concealed blade. His network spans from the ports to the backrooms of Ikoyi, and he knows where every bribe goes.
npc.quote: In Lagos, everything has a price — even your conscience.
dialogue: Al Habtoor? That’s where foreign eyes look in and see luxury — but we know where the real gold flows after midnight.
These military boys, they wear uniforms but their pockets are lined with the same dirty currency as the rest of us.
When the pressure’s on and the generators die, I don’t panic — I count my blessings and my bullets.
